BURSEVI:v3p28/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r1.speaker: السري السقطي
BURSEVI:v3p28/r1.claim: Al-Sarī al-Saqaṭī says he found Bahlūl in a cemetery; Bahlūl replied that the dead do not harm him or gossip when he is away.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r2.speaker: بهلول
BURSEVI:v3p28/r2.claim: Bahlūl left when hungry and recited that hunger is a pious act and prolonged hunger will eventually be followed by satisfaction.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28/r3.claim: A king's parable shows God adorning chosen lovers with righteous deeds and pure states: they need not display themselves to ordinary people, since God knows and their rank will be seen at the great gathering.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28/r4.claim: A Persian couplet contrasts the noble servants of God with the speaker's group as wretched slaves.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28/r5.claim: Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor wool-clad believers such as Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and Salmān so they could retain his company and status before Arab visitors.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r6.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v3p28/r6.claim: The Prophet refused to expel believers, though he considered separating them to attract Quraysh; revelation taught that religion does not privilege the rich over the poor.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28/r7.claim: Expulsion means removal; morning and evening remembrance signifies continuity, and whoever remembers continually remains with God.

BURSEVI:v3p28/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v3p28/r8.claim: The Prophet says, ‘I am the companion of whoever remembers Me.’

BURSEVI:v3p28/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28/r9.claim: The poor worshippers seek God's face and pleasure alone, not worldly aims.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r1.claim: ‘Seeking His face’ is circumstantial to ‘they call’; it stresses that sincerity is the essential point of supplication.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r2.claim: A Persian couplet says worship is good when intention is sincere; without that, it is like a kernel-less grain.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r3.claim: Seeking God's face is among the strongest grounds for honor and is incompatible with expelling poor worshippers.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r4.claim: Quraysh not only disparaged poor believers' status but alleged their faith was false and that they gathered for food and clothing; God rejects this as grounds for expulsion.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r5.claim: The Prophet must judge by their outward mark of piety; any hidden defect in faith harms only them, not him, so he should welcome and nurture them.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r6.claim: The repeated denial of responsibility emphasizes that their reckoning is no concern of the Prophet, just as his is no concern of theirs.

BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r7.speaker: أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v3p28#2/r7.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd says the repeated phrase emphasizes the point by pairing it with the uncontroversial reverse; ‘then you expel them’ answers the prohibition's logic.

BURSEVI:v3p29/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p29/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p29/r1.claim: ‘Thus We tested them’ points to God's giving poor believers precedence in religion by granting faith despite their poor worldly condition, while the rich had worldly precedence.

BURSEVI:v3p29/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p29/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p29/r2.claim: The prefixed kāf intensifies the demonstrative: God tried them with a complete and remarkable trial.

QASHANI:6:52-53/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:52-53/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:52-53/r1.claim: The dawn and dusk callers are complete people of unity; warnings benefit neither them, lost in God, nor those whose hearts are hardened.

QASHANI:6:52-53/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:52-53/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:52-53/r2.claim: Their constant worship is presence of heart, witnessing of spirit, and orientation of the secret to God alone through eternal love, without seeking reward or fearing punishment.

QASHANI:6:52-53/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:52-53/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:52-53/r3.claim: They seek God's Essence rather than changing attributes or intermediaries, having witnessed the annihilation of means and even of their own selves.

QASHANI:6:52-53/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:52-53/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:52-53/r4.claim: They have no intermediary relation of account through the Prophet and, absorbed in God, do not involve themselves in his mission, aid to Islam, or opposition to disbelief.

QASHANI:6:52-53/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:52-53/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:52-53/r5.claim: Expelling them distracts their uninterrupted presence and makes the Prophet unjust; the following trial is that veiled people see only poverty and outward appearance and scorn their hidden rank.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r2.claim: Having no protector or intercessor besides God means relying neither on other creatures nor on one’s own deeds or states, but on divine care and mercy.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r3.claim: The command protects the poor and vulnerable companions after some people sought to remove them from the Prophet’s gathering; God took their side and showed the effect of humble prayer.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r4.claim: The Prophet should look past their ragged outward appearance to the burning longing in their inner lives.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r5.claim: God made their inward state public and testified that they sought His face; without that testimony no one could confidently claim that a creature seeks God.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r6.claim: In strict theology, will attaches to originated things, whereas God’s eternal, self-subsisting essence is beyond origination; this divine desire is not ordinary choice or merely a lexical sense.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r7.claim: The most precise account of spiritual desire is a need arising in the heart that robs the seeker of rest until reaching God.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r8.claim: A poem depicts longing overcoming a traveler who crosses wilderness without fear of lions or wolves.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r9.claim: Morning and evening limit the companions’ outward acts, but their inward desire for God’s face lasts without interruption; the phrase about seeking His face is circumstantial.

QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p295/r10.claim: They have no worldly or afterlife request and no concern beyond their Master; having devoted themselves to God, they receive His devoted care.

QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r1.claim: The poor are light in burden; God, rather than the Prophet or the companions, takes account of each person and gives each the outcome of his deeds.

QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r2.claim: The superior should be grateful and the lesser patient; in love, gratitude is the lesser person’s path and can equal the superior’s gratitude.

QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p296/r3.claim: Two poems express gratitude even for a beloved’s blame or harm, because the beloved’s name and actions remain precious.

QIRAAT-ER:6:52:8#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:6:52:8#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:6:52:8#1/r1.claim: Ghudwa as an instance noun contrasts with ghadāh as general morning, shifting from habitual to specific morning.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p207#5/r1.claim: Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to expel Bilal, Salman, Suhayb, and other poor Muslims whose smell bothered him, promising to follow if they were removed; the verse forbade it.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p208/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p208/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p208/r1.claim: Qatada says Quraysh unbelievers also asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslims so they would follow him; God instead described the believers as those who remember Him morning and evening.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p208/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p208/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p208/r2.claim: The statement that God tested some people by others means that He tried them through one another.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p496/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p496/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p496/r1.claim: This segment reproduces Quranic verses 6:36–52 without commentary.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p497/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p497/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p497/r4.claim: Ṭard means expulsion accompanied by humiliation; ṭarīd means an expelled person, and the author notes tribal names derived from these terms.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r4.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas says the verse was revealed about six poor believers, including himself, Ibn Masʿud, Suhayb, ʿAmmar, al-Miqdad, and Bilal, after Quraysh demanded their expulsion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r5.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r5.claim: Khabbab says the verse concerned weak believers whom the Prophet taught morning and evening; elite visitors al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna objected to sitting with them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r6.claim: The author doubts this version because the verse is Meccan while those elites were not warned until Medina.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r7.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r7.claim: A related report says the Prophet would rise and leave the poor believers, after which the instruction to remain with those who call on God was revealed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r8.claim: Al-ʿAwfi's report from Ibn ʿAbbas says nobles would believe if the poor were moved back so they could pray behind the nobles; expulsion meant moving them from the row, not the gathering.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p520/r9.claim: Despite variations in the reports, their common point is that Arab notables asked the Prophet to send the poor believers away, prompting the verse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r1.claim: After commanding warning for the unpious, God honors the pious and forbids their expulsion, describing their outward and inward sincerity in worship.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r2.claim: Calling on their Lord means asking, seeking refuge, and directing supplication and desire to Him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r3.claim: Morning and evening stand for continual worship, like saying 'praise God morning and evening'; they may also be singled out because they are busy hours, making remembrance then especially telling.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Muqatil identify the phrase with the two daily prayers practiced in Mecca, morning and evening.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r5.claim: Qatada and Mujahid in one report identify the phrase as the dawn and afternoon prayers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid in another report, and Ibrahim identify the phrase with the five prayers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r7.speaker: بعض القصاص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r7.claim: Some storytellers take it as people gathering with the believers morning and evening; Ibn al-Musayyib, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAmra, and others object that the verse concerns congregational prayers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r8.claim: Abu Jaʿfar interprets it as reciting and learning the Qur'an.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r9.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r9.claim: Al-Dahhak says it means worship; Ibrahim in another report says remembrance of God; al-Zajjaj says monotheistic, sincere supplication and worship.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r10.speaker: ابن عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r10.claim: The majority read بالغداة; Ibn ʿAmir and several others read بالغدوة, Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman is also reported without the final هاء, and Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads plural forms بالغدوات والعشيات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p521/r11.claim: The familiar form غدوة is treated as a proper noun and diptote; al-Farra reports a dialect that uses it for the morning of the same day.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r1.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r1.claim: Abu Zayd attests غدوة for the morning of the current day; Sibawayh and al-Khalil also report a dialect that declines it with tanwin.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r2.claim: Abu ʿUbayd faults Ibn ʿAmir and al-Sulami's reading as following the written waw, arguing that script does not prove pronunciation, as in صلاة and زكاة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r3.claim: The author rebukes Abu ʿUbayd for ignorance of the dialect and reading transmission, defending the readers' competence and the principle that recitation is transmitted orally.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r4.claim: Al-ʿAshiyy is apparently synonymous with al-ʿashiyya, though it may be a collective; the cited verse uses it for late afternoon.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r5.claim: يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ means they make their intentions sincere for God in worship; 'face' can denote a thing's essence and reality.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains seeking God's face as seeking His reward.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r7.claim: The phrase يريدون وجهه is circumstantial; theologians who use 'His face' to prove a bodily member are mistaken.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r8.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and the majority understand 'their reckoning' and 'your reckoning' as the reckoning of deeds.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r9.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r9.claim: Al-Tabari transmits an interpretation of reckoning as worldly provision: the Prophet neither provides for them nor they for him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the statement answers attacks on poor believers' sincerity: the Prophet must judge by their outward conduct, and each person bears their own account, as in the rule that no bearer bears another's burden.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p522/r11.claim: The author rejects al-Zamakhshari's hypothetical that their inner state might be blameworthy, since God has already testified to their sincere intentions.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the paired clauses together mean that neither side is held to the other's reckoning, echoing the rule that no soul bears another's burden.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r2.claim: The author says al-Zamakhshari's wording لا تؤاخذ أنت ولا هم بحساب صاحبه is ungrammatical because no singular antecedent supports its pronoun; he proposes clearer alternatives.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r3.claim: The apparent pronouns throughout the two clauses refer to the poor believers who call on God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the pronouns to refer to the polytheists, making the clauses parenthetical: the Prophet's account is not theirs, so their belief should not lead him to expel believers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise allows the pronouns to mean the disbelievers seeking the poor believers' expulsion, while تطردهم refers to the weak believers; the following ف supports a causal link.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r6.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523/r6.claim: Al-Tabari says reckoning here concerns worldly provision, in which case all pronouns refer to the believers.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r1.claim: The first من is partitive and circumstantial: if it followed شيء it would be adjectival; عليک is the predicate under the Hijazi analysis, or the subject predicate otherwise.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r2.claim: Making the second من حسابك circumstantial is weak because a semantic عامل cannot normally have its حال advanced before both itself and its possessor; other predicate analyses are also weak because عليهم carries the main information.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r3.claim: The two clauses honor the Prophet by placing him first both times, although the second could have been phrased with the believers first; this is reciprocal framing (رد العجز على الصدر).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r4.claim: The apparent فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ responds to the negation: since their reckoning is not the Prophet's concern, expulsion cannot follow from it; the first possible sense of ما تأتينا فتحدثنا does not fit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r5.claim: فتكون is coordinated with فتطردهم, reporting the nonoccurrence of both expulsion and its consequence, wrongdoing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p523#2/r6.claim: Another parsing makes فتكون a response to the prohibition لا تطرد, with the two account clauses interrupting between prohibition and result.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p524/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p524/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p524/r1.claim: On the prohibitive parsing, the account clauses and the response to the first are parenthetical before the result of the ban on expelling them.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p524/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p524/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p524/r2.claim: The unjust are people who put things in the wrong place.

SULAMI:v1p199#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r1.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r1.claim: The way of the spiritual seeker is continual remembrance and sincere action; elders advise treating such seekers gently and overlooking their slips.

SULAMI:v1p199#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r2.claim: A servant should remain in the reality of remembrance and keep the inner secret pure, recognizing God as the originator and the end.

SULAMI:v1p199#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r3.claim: Do not distance those adorned with the beauty of servanthood, whose days are devoted to turning toward God.

SULAMI:v1p199#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الفارسي
SULAMI:v1p199#2/r4.claim: Desiring God means remembering Him continually; the sincere seeker is recognized by being averse to unlike companions and seeking his own kind.

TUSTARI:6:52/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r1.claim: Those who seek God’s face seek His approval and are never absent from Him for an hour.

TUSTARI:6:52/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r2.claim: The most ascetic people are those whose food is purest.

TUSTARI:6:52/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r3.claim: The most devout people work hardest at keeping God’s commands and prohibitions.

TUSTARI:6:52/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r4.claim: The people most beloved to God are most sincere toward His creatures.

TUSTARI:6:52/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r5.claim: Sahl defines a wasted lifespan as one that is squandered.

TUSTARI:6:52/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r6.claim: Inwardly, the verse describes a servant directing every movement and stillness toward God, as in the description of those who respond to their Lord.

TUSTARI:6:52/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r7.claim: Experiencing both the seeking servant and the one sought is a favor from God, who joins them in saying every blessing comes from Him.

TUSTARI:6:52/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r8.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r8.claim: The seeker exerts intention, worship, and effort to find God’s path and remains in pursuit; the one sought receives God’s enabling, performs obedience without strain, and then rises through higher stations.

TUSTARI:6:52/r9.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:6:52/r9.speaker: author
TUSTARI:6:52/r9.claim: The stations are found in the angels’ description: each has a known station.

AKHFASH:v1p299#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p299#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p299#2/r1.claim: One parse makes فتطردهم an accusative consequence of the statement that neither party is accountable for the other.

AKHFASH:v1p299#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p299#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p299#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, فتطردهم is linked as an accusative consequence to the prohibition ولا تطرد, followed by فتكون من الظالمين.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r1.claim: After commanding the Prophet to warn the people who may become pious, God forbids doing so in a way that would lead him to expel the poor believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r2.claim: Some accounts suggest the warning and no-expulsion verses came down together, while others do not indicate that.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports Quraysh leaders seeing Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and other poor Muslims with the Prophet and demanding their expulsion, promising they might then follow him; the Quran was revealed concerning this.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r1.speaker: خباب
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna looked down on the poor believers and demanded private access for tribal leaders, promising to meet the Prophet with the poor later; after Gabriel delivered the verse, the Prophet called the believers to him and then stayed with them when rising.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have Muhammad expel poor slaves and allies so they would follow him; Umar suggested doing so temporarily, and verses warning and identifying the grateful were revealed, after which Umar apologized.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r3.claim: The report names the poor believers as Bilal, ʿAmmar, Salim, Subayh, Ibn Masʿud, al-Miqdad, Waqid, ʿAmr, and Marthad, with allies and freedmen among them.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r4.claim: The report says the verse 'Thus We have tried some of them by others' addressed Quraysh leaders and their clients; when it came, Umar apologized, and 'When those who believe in Our signs come to you' was revealed.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p158#3/r5.claim: Al-ghadah derives from ghudwah with the waw changing to alif; al-ashi derives from ashwa with waw changing to ya and assimilation. The author says al-ashi appears singular like ashiyyah, though some call it a plural.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r1.claim: Some say al-ashi is a plural of ashiyyah, but the author finds this far-fetched; morning means early morning or the time from dawn prayer until sunrise, and evening means the end of the day.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r2.claim: Morning and evening can denote continual practice, or the acts of supplication, prayer, remembrance, or Qur'an recitation; the temporal terms can stand for what occurs at those times, and prayer can also mean its time or place.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets morning and evening as the dawn and afternoon prayers; the times are named for the prayers, which are singled out for their honor.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAmir, also in al-Kahf, and several other readers recite الغدوة with a wāw; Abu ʿUbayd calls that reading an error because he treats ghudwah as a proper name that cannot take the article.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r5.claim: The author rejects Abu Ubayd criticism: ghudwah is also attested as a common noun with the article, as reported from al-Khalil by Sibawayh, al-Mubarrad, and other language authorities; the transmitted reading itself suffices as evidence.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r6.claim: The verse does not establish that the Prophet actually expelled anyone; reports say he considered assigning separate times to the devoted poor and Quraysh leaders to draw the latter toward faith, without humiliating the believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r7.speaker: المشهور
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r7.claim: The common interpretation takes God's face as His essence, hence the believers seek Him sincerely; the author notes that this interpretation must explain how God can be willed if will attaches only to possible things.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r8.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets God's face as the direction or path He commands them to seek.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p159/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes seeking God's face as a metaphor for love and seeking His approval; the author says this account is questionable.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r1.claim: The word 'face' may be used for honor or emphasis, as in expressions such as 'the face of an argument'; the believers seek God in this sense.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r2.speaker: عطاء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r2.claim: The plural pronoun in 'their account' refers to the poor believers, as reported from ʿAṭāʾ and most commentators; grammatically, من is an added marker of comprehensiveness, and the clause interrupts the prohibition to support it.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r3.claim: The believers' faith and deeds are not the Prophet's concern to judge; he must apply rulings to outward appearances and leave hidden accounts to God, against the taunts resembling Noah's people's complaint.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the account as their provision: their poverty would not harm the Prophet, so it cannot justify expelling them.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the two reciprocal denials as one thought like 'no bearer bears another's burden'; the author objects that this is not a fitting reading of the Qur'anic wording.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r6.claim: Fronting 'upon you' in both clauses may honor the Prophet or emphasize that the believers' account is not exclusively his responsibility.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r7.claim: Some commentators, including a report from Ibn Abbas, take the plural pronoun to mean the idolaters: the Prophet is not accountable for them, so concern for their conversion cannot prompt him to expel believers.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p160/r8.claim: The pronoun in 'then you would expel them' refers to the believers under either reading; the subjunctive presents expulsion as a consequence ruled out by the preceding denial.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r1.speaker: الإمام والزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r1.claim: Al-Razi and al-Zamakhshari allow 'then you would be among the wrongdoers' to coordinate with the preceding consequence, since expelling the believers would cause wrongdoing.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r2.claim: The author answers that injustice through expulsion ceases when expulsion is negated, so the coordinated clauses share the same cause for their subjunctive form.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r3.claim: An objection says the coordination implies that expulsion would not be wrong if the Prophet were accountable for them; the reply reads the denial as saying that lack of responsibility is why expulsion would wrong them.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r4.speaker: الدر المصون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r4.claim: A further parsing makes the first result clause answer the prohibition, but the author finds the literal repetition 'do not expel them and then you would expel them' untenable.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r5.claim: The second denial cannot govern the result if that would imply that expulsion is proper whenever the Prophet bears their account; because that meaning is impossible, the first denial governs.

ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p161/r6.claim: The warning that he would be among wrongdoers means wronging himself or those believers, or becoming characterized by injustice.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r4.claim: Salman and Khabbab say the verse came after al-Aqra, Uyayna, and their elite group asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers such as Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, and Khabbab, whose coarse wool clothes they despised.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r5.claim: When the elites demanded a separate meeting and a written promise to remove the poor men, the Prophet refused to drive believers away; Gabriel brought this verse and the command to keep company with those seeking God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r6.claim: The Prophet dropped the sheet, summoned the poor believers, and honored them with God's message of mercy; he thereafter sat close to them and waited for them before leaving.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p145#2/r7.claim: The Prophet told them he was grateful not to die before being commanded to remain patient with members of his community, saying their life and death were with them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the petitioners proposed separate days or a single gathering where the Prophet would face them and turn his back on the poor; God revealed the prohibition against dismissing the poor worshippers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r2.claim: Mujahid says Quraysh claimed they would follow Muhammad if not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd; the verse followed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says morning and evening worship means the dawn and afternoon prayers; he also reports that it can mean all five prayers after elite men asked the poor to pray behind them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r4.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib rejects reading the phrase as a session for public storytellers; he says it refers to the prayer they had just completed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r5.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai interprets the phrase as remembering God; another view takes it as literal supplication.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r6.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking God through obedience; Ibn Abbas says they seek God's reward.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r7.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for the worshippers' account and they are not responsible for his; their livelihood is not his burden, nor is his provision theirs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p146/r8.claim: The phrase 'so you would drive them away' answers the preceding negation; 'then you would be among wrongdoers' answers the prohibition, respectively.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r1.claim: After commanding warning for the heedless, God commands honoring and drawing near the devout, rather than expelling them to appease Quraysh.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r2.speaker: قريش
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r2.claim: Quraysh offered to sit and talk with the Prophet if he expelled the poor Muslim worshippers, including Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Salman.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r3.claim: The Prophet first said he would not drive away believers; when the request was repeated, he agreed to make them rise when Quraysh arrived.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r4.speaker: عمر
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r4.claim: Umar asked the Prophet to do this temporarily so they could see what the visitors would do; as a document and Ali were brought to write, the verse was revealed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r5.claim: Mentioning morning and evening can mean continuous worship, or the dawn and afternoon prayers; Ibn Amir reads ghudwah here and in al-Kahf.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r6.claim: The worshippers seek God's face sincerely; making sincerity the qualification shows its centrality, and the prohibition consequently requires honoring them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r7.claim: The accounting clause may mean the Prophet is not responsible for their faith or inner sincerity, even if their inner state is as the pagans alleged; their account is theirs and his is his.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r8.claim: Another view takes their account as their livelihood and poverty; a further view takes the pronouns to refer to the pagans, who are not accountable for the Prophet's account or vice versa.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:52/r9.claim: Expelling the worshippers would make the Prophet one of the wrongdoers; the final clause answers the prohibition or follows from expelling as its consequence.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r5.claim: Those the Prophet must not drive away are poor Muslims, devoted to their Lord in contrast to unbelievers who call on powerless beings.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r6.claim: Morning and evening may mean both ends of each day, the two daily prayers, or continuous worship; their long constancy indicates sincerity rather than ostentation.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r7.claim: The wealthy polytheists promised to follow Muhammad if he expelled his humble companions, whom they disparaged as insincere and driven by need.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r8.claim: The Prophet has no stake in worldly gain from expelling the poor or accepting the rich; his mission calls people away from worldly life.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p642/r9.claim: The denial of responsibility for one another's account means the Prophet sees only outward conduct; he need not expel them over a fear that they are insincere or that they burden him.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r1.claim: An alternative reading of the denial of mutual accounting, linked to 18:28, concerns provision: the Prophet's invitation is for the afterlife, and neither the poor nor the Prophet depends on the other's provision.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r2.claim: The author adduces lexicons and usage showing that hisab can mean sufficiency or provision: 78:36 gives an abundant gift; the verb can mean feeding to satisfaction; and a report from Simak says hosts did not honor their guest.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد الهروي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd explains ahsabtuhu as giving someone enough until he says, “That suffices me.”

BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r4.claim: The phrase “without account” in 2:212 means without stinting or constriction; Ibn Faris likewise glosses ahsabtuhu as giving enough or what satisfies.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p643/r5.claim: Expelling the poor would be unjustly putting things out of place and would not make the wealthy polytheists believe; guidance belongs to God alone.

DURR-FULL:v3p272/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p272/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v3p272/r3.claim: Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslim companions such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so that they might follow him; the warning verse was revealed.

DURR-FULL:v3p272/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p272/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v3p272/r4.claim: Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have Muhammad expel poor and enslaved followers so they would join; Umar suggested testing their request, then verses about not expelling the believers were revealed.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r1.speaker: خباب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that two Quraysh leaders looked down on the poor believers around the Prophet and asked for a privileged private audience; Gabriel revealed the prohibition on expelling them, and the Prophet discarded the written request.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r2.claim: Sa'd says the verse was revealed about six people, including himself and Ibn Masud, with a command to bring them near.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1297/r3.claim: Al-Rabi says leaders objected to Salman, Suhayb, and Bilal occupying the Prophet's gathering; God forbade expelling them and the verse refers to Salman and his companions.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says those who call upon their Lord are worshipping Him.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r2.claim: Ibrahim identifies them as people devoted to remembrance of God.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r3.claim: Abu Jafar says the Prophet would sit with these believers and teach them the Quran.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the morning gathering as the obligatory dawn prayer; similar explanations identify the times with prescribed prayers.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the evening gathering as the obligatory afternoon prayer.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r6.speaker: عمرو بن شعيب
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r6.claim: Amr ibn Shuaib identifies the evening prayer in the phrase as the Isha prayer.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r7.claim: Mujahid says Quraysh objected to Bilal and Ibn Umm Maktum's presence, but the Prophet was forbidden to dismiss them; the passage continues through 6:53.

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1298/r8.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says expelling those believers would itself make the Prophet one of the wrongdoers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r1.claim: The command coordinates with the warning in 6:51: the Prophet is to stay with those fearing resurrection despite the arrogance of leading polytheists.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r2.claim: The renewed relative description suits the ruling better than a pronoun: those who continually invoke God sincerely deserve the Prophet's company as callers to God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r3.claim: In Muslim's report, six companions were with the Prophet when polytheists asked him to expel them; Sa'd names himself, Ibn Mas'ud, a Hudhayli, Bilal, and two unnamed men, after which the verse was revealed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r4.speaker: الواحدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi identifies the four unnamed companions in Sa'd's account as Suhayb, Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r5.speaker: البيهقي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqi's fuller account says Quraysh chiefs proposed removing poor believers while they visited and restoring them afterward; the Prophet refused, then agreed to the arrangement hoping they would believe, and the verse came.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r6.speaker: ابن ماجة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r6.claim: A report in Ibn Majah, from Khabbab, names al-Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn as the men who made the expulsion request and cause of revelation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the Ibn Majah attribution unlikely because this is a Meccan verse and the two men came with the Banu Tamim delegation in Medina.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p245/r8.claim: The two men may have made a similar request later, and the Prophet answered it with the verse originally revealed about an analogous proposal.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r1.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for whether polytheists believe; their account belongs elsewhere, so he must not deprive believers of their rights to secure others' conversion.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r2.claim: The genitive in 'their accounting' can mean either the Prophet's reckoning of them or the polytheists' reckoning of believers' poverty and weakness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r3.claim: The fronted predicate with عَلَى conveys obligation or burden and corrects a possible inclination to yield to Quraysh's chiefs.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r4.claim: The preposition من is redundant for emphasis, specifying the comprehensive scope of the negation under لا.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r5.claim: Fronting the predicates is optional because the following indefinite subjects occur under negation; it may convey emphasis or restriction, and al-Kashshaf favors restriction.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r6.claim: On the restrictive reading, only God accounts for the believers; the negated account is confined to the Prophet, as in the restrictive reading of 37:47.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p249/r7.claim: A poetic example uses أحرزوا for the polytheists' seizure of the Muslims' collected spoils.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r1.claim: The verse accumulates five emphases: two uses of من, fronting, restrictive wording, and completion by negating the reciprocal account, to utterly disavow yielding to the request.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r2.claim: The address indirectly exposes Quraysh chiefs' claim that poor believers kept them from the Prophet; if sincere, they should attend without judging others, as clarified in 6:55.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r3.claim: The implied affirmative counterpart is that each person is accountable for himself; no believer should lose a right to satisfy the Prophet or someone seeking faith.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p250/r4.claim: The warning resembles the conditional address in which even the Prophet's work would be void if he associated partners with God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r1.claim: The reciprocal clause indirectly accuses the polytheists of disguising pride as advice, pretending expulsion would win them over while claiming concern for the Prophet.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r2.claim: The meaning is not that both groups' accounts belong to God: that reading is out of context and makes the second clause redundant, unlike Noah's reported statement.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r3.claim: Alternatively, fronting may simply emphasize that the Prophet bears no obligation, since restriction does not clearly fit the believers who invoke God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251/r4.claim: The reciprocal clause is added to complete the rationale; the first clause receives priority because its application to the Prophet and the requesters is the main point.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r1.claim: The repeated verb is a subjunctive result of the prohibition; repeating expulsion reinforces the command and reconnects it to the later warning after intervening material.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r2.claim: The verb may instead answer the preceding negation: do not expel them merely to satisfy their enemies' wish.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r3.claim: Being among wrongdoers follows from expelling believers to please others; the threat also characterizes the requesters as proud people disposed to injustice.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p251#2/r4.claim: A second parsing makes 'you would be among wrongdoers' the result of the prohibition, with the repeated expulsion clause serving as a resumptive link after a long interruption.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r1.claim: Most read بالغداة; Ibn ʿĀmir and several named readers use بالغدوة with ḍamma, still dāl, and fatḥa on wāw, also in al-Kahf; غدوة is normally a proper-name form.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r2.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says Arabs do not add the article to definite الغدوة and cites ‘غداة الخميس’; the author says this misses an indefinite dialect form.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayd attacks بالغدوة as copying the written wāw, which cannot establish pronunciation because الصلاة and الزكاة are written with wāw but pronounced without it.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī prefers بالغداة: it can be indefinite or definite with the article, while غدوة is a proper name and should not take the article; its written wāw proves nothing.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52/r5.claim: The author rejects Abū ʿUbayd’s attack: these respected Arab readers are not presumed mistaken, and Sibawayh and al-Khalīl record indefinite غدوة.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r1.claim: العشي is indefinite; whether it is synonymous with feminine عشية or a collective like قمح/قمحة is disputed, and the first is likelier because 38:31 refers to one evening.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r2.claim: Regional codices all write الغدوة with wāw, but Ibn ʿĀmir’s reading rests on transmission, not spelling alone; forms such as الصلاة and الزكاة are read without wāw.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r3.claim: غداة derives from غدوة by opening wāw and changing it to alif; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads plural الغدوات والعشيات, while another report has بالغدو with doubled wāw and no tāʾ.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r4.claim: They report that some Arabs make غدوة indefinite with tanwin, comparable to ضحوة; Ibn ʿĀmir makes it indefinite and adds the article.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows the article on غدوة by treating a definite word as indefinite, like فينة when it means ‘time after time.’

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r6.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says غدوة is normally definite but may be indefinite and then take the article; he lists readers who use this form.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r7.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#2/r7.claim: Makkī says غداة is always indefinite; most Arabs make غدوة definite, while a minority make it indefinite, supporting the reading.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r1.claim: يريدون is circumstantial from either the subject or object of يدعون; the subject analysis is correct, with omitted sense ‘they seek His face through their supplication at these times.’

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r2.claim: In ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء, ما may govern an accusative predicate عليك, or be inactive with عليك a fronted predicate and من شيء its subject with extra من.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r3.claim: من حسابهم may be a partitive circumstantial phrase modifying شيء because a delayed modifier would be adjectival; it then depends on the implicit ‘being’ in عليك.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#3/r4.claim: Alternatively من شيء is a subject raised by عليك under negation, with من حسابهم circumstantial; or من حسابهم is predicate and عليك circumstantial, though this last information structure is unclear.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r1.claim: In the parallel clause من حسابك cannot readily be a circumstance before its semantic governor and owner, so it may be explanatory instead; its partitive sense is also unclear.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r2.claim: Addressing the Prophet first in both clauses honors him; the second could have repeated the first word order, but is rearranged in context.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r3.claim: The two clauses use the rhetorical figure رد الأعجاز على الصدور, also found in the cited proverb and poem.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the clauses together mean neither person is accountable for the other’s account, echoing 6:164; both are needed to express reciprocity.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r5.claim: Al-Shaykh calls al-Zamakhsharī’s wording ungrammatical because صاحبه lacks a compatible singular antecedent, whether the pronoun is read as third or second person.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#4/r6.claim: The intended wording can be repaired by supplying كل واحد with أنت ولا هم appositional to it; however, the point is that each is not charged for another’s account.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r1.claim: The people addressed were poor, socially weak believers, including Bilal, Ammar, Ibn Umm Abd, Murthid al-Ghanawi, Khabbab, Suhayb, Subayh, Dhul-Shimalayn, and al-Miqdad.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r2.claim: Some unbelievers said their status and rank prevented them from mixing with the poor; if Muhammad expelled them, the elites would follow him. A report also attributes the advice to Abu Talib, and Quraysh leaders gathered to press it; the author thinks the proposal was likely a ruse.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says some unbelievers asked to move the poor believers out of the front prayer row so they could take their places and believe.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r4.speaker: خباب بن الأرت عن الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r4.claim: Al-Tabari transmits that al-Aqraʿ ibn Habis and similar Arab notables asked for a separate meeting without slaves or allies and for a written agreement; Muhammad considered it before the verse came down.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.claim: Al-Mahdawi says all the pronouns in the passage refer to the believers; Hasan says their accounting concerns their deeds, as most interpreters hold.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.claim: The first min is partitive and the second is emphatic; the two fa-verbs follow the prior negation and prohibition, and being among wrongdoers means putting things in the wrong place.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.claim: The apparent reading returns all three pronouns to one group: those who call upon their Lord.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.claim: Al-Tabari also takes all three pronouns as referring to the worshippers, but understands their account as worldly provision.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya refer the first two pronouns to the polytheists and the third to the worshippers.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.claim: Another view refers the pronouns in their account and upon them to the polytheists, making the two clauses parenthetical.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.claim: The two clauses can be parenthetical regardless of whom the first two pronouns refer to; they interrupt the prohibition and its result.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.claim: The subjunctive فتطردهم can answer the prohibition or express the consequence of the negated mutual accounting; the intended sense denies both expulsion and its cause.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.claim: The alternative reading of the example, where the visit occurs but the conversation does not, does not suit this verse.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.claim: فتكون is most clearly coordinated with فتطردهم, reporting expulsion and the injustice that results from it.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows coordination, treating being unjust as caused by expelling them.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.speaker: مكي والواحدي وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.claim: Makki, al-Wahidi, and Abu al-Baqa mention فتكون as a response to the prohibition.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan compares this construction with the prohibition in Ta-Ha 20:61 and treats the intervening clauses as parenthetical.

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.claim: The parenthetical analysis does not depend on referring the first two pronouns to the polytheists.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.claim: The verse concerned six poor Companions, including Sa'd, Ibn Masud, Suhayb, Ammar, al-Miqdad, and Bilal; Quraysh demanded the Prophet expel them rather than be seen following them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.claim: Khabbab says poor believers learned from the Prophet morning and evening; al-Aqra and Uyayna demanded they be removed, then pressed for a written agreement, until Gabriel brought the warning against expelling them and the Prophet welcomed them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.claim: Quraysh leaders passing by the Prophet and poor Companions asked whether he expected them to become followers of those men.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.claim: Nobles of Abd Manaf asked Abu Talib to make Muhammad expel clients and slaves; Umar suggested trying it, but the verse came and Umar apologized.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.claim: The verse concerns the clients Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Mihja, Salman, Amir ibn Fuhayra, and Salim, and another verse also addressed them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.claim: Some nobles offered belief if the Prophet delayed the poor believers and let them pray behind the nobles; this report seeks moving them from the prayer row, unlike the others' request to remove them from his gathering.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.claim: Calling upon their Lord means the obligatory prayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as the five daily prayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.claim: Another report from Mujahid and Qatada identifies the prayers as dawn and afternoon.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.claim: Muqatil says prayer at that time was two units at dawn and two at evening, before the five daily prayers were prescribed.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.claim: Another interpretation of calling on God is remembering Him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.claim: Another interpretation is learning the Qur'an morning and evening.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.claim: Another interpretation is praying to God with monotheism, sincerity, and worship.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.claim: Most readers say bil-ghadah; Ibn Amir reads bil-ghudwah here and in al-Kahf 18:28. Farra sees ghudwah as inherently definite, Abu Ali says ghadah can take the article while ghudwah is a proper name, and al-Khalil permits it as a time word like duha.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.claim: Morning stands for the whole day and evening for the night; if a person's daytime worship is sincere, nighttime worship is even purer.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.claim: Those who seek God's face seek God Himself, and God attests to the sincerity of their intentions.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.claim: The account mentioned here is an account of deeds.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.claim: Other interpretations of the account mentioned are provision or sufficiency: neither group is responsible for providing for the other.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.claim: The warning not to expel them threatens inclusion among the wrongdoers because the Prophet had considered giving the leaders precedence over the weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.claim: Do not drive away people who invoke God morning and evening seeking His face; keep them close as companions, as also commanded in 18:28.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatada say the morning and evening invocation refers to the obligatory prayers.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.claim: Invoking God means worshipping and asking Him; 40:60 similarly says to call upon God and He will respond.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.claim: Seeking God’s face means that these worshippers sincerely seek His favor through their worship and obedience.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.claim: Neither the Prophet nor these worshippers answer for one another; Ibn Kathir compares Noah’s response that their account belongs to God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.claim: Seeking God’s face means that these people sincerely seek His favor through their worship and obedience.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.claim: Neither the Prophet nor these worshippers answer for one another; Ibn Kathir compares Noah’s response that their account belongs to God.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.speaker: خباب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.claim: Khabbab says al-Aqra and Uyayna disdained the poor believers and sought an exclusive meeting with the Prophet; Gabriel revealed the command not to expel them, and the Prophet discarded their written pledge.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.claim: Al-Hakim grades Sa’d’s report about six Companions according to the criteria of al-Bukhari and Muslim; Ibn Hibban also transmits its route.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Jarir also transmits the earlier report through Asbat.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report strange because this verse is Meccan whereas al-Aqra and Uyayna converted long after the Hijra.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.speaker: سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.claim: Sa’d says the verse concerned six Companions, including Ibn Masud, who arrived early and drew near to hear the Prophet; Quraysh objected to their proximity.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads بالغدوة والعشي with wāw and a ḍamma on ghayn in both this verse and al-Kahf; the other readers have alif and fatḥa.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the plural forms بالغدوات والعشيات; the original wāw turns into alif after fatḥa on the preceding dāl.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.claim: Ṭard means banishing, exclusion, or expulsion.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.claim: Wajh can mean the familiar bodily face or the essence/aspect of a thing, as in saying this is the wajh of an opinion.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.claim: The prohibition طرد is jussive, with kasra to separate adjacent vowelless consonants; فتطردهم can answer the negation in ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء.

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.claim: Abū Muslim parses فتطردهم فتكون as consequences of the prohibition: do not expel them, or you become unjust by expelling them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.claim: After warning those Muslims who are not yet devout, the text turns to the devout: draw them near and honor them, and do not obey those seeking the opposite.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.claim: Calling on their Lord morning and evening means continuous worship; alternatively it specifically means the dawn and afternoon prayers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r3.claim: Seeking God's face denotes sincerity; ‘face’ can express a thing's essence and reality.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.speaker: رؤسا من المشركين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.claim: Polytheist leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor believers such as Ammar, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab, and Salman so they could speak with him; he refused, then briefly considered their request in hope they might believe, before revelation forbade it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.speaker: سلمان وخباب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.claim: Salman and Khabbab say this was revealed about them: the Prophet sat very close, then revelation told him to remain with them until they rose; he praised God for living to receive that command.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.claim: The accounting clauses assure the Prophet that allegations about the believers do not bind him: he judges outward signs, and any hidden fault remains their burden, as in the rule that no bearer bears another's burden.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.claim: Both accounting clauses are needed together to convey that neither group is answerable for the other's account.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.claim: Another view takes the pronouns to refer to the polytheists: they are not responsible for the Prophet's account nor he for theirs, so eagerness for their conversion must not lead him to expel believers.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.claim: In the syntax, فتطردهم responds to the negation and فتكون to the prohibition; alternatively, it coordinates as a consequence because injustice results from expelling them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.claim: Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to expel weak believers including Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Ibn Masud, promising to follow if he did; Umar urged a trial, and the Prophet considered it before the verse came down.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpret those calling on their Lord morning and evening as performing the five prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai interprets calling on their Lord as remembrance of God; other views say Qur'an recitation or worship.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.claim: Abu Jafar interprets the devotional calling as honoring the Qur'an; al-Dahhak says it is worship of God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.claim: Seeking God's face may mean intending Him, since Arabic uses face for the thing itself to magnify it, or seeking His obedience by aiming toward what He directs.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says each person answers for their own deeds, so neither group bears the other's reward or punishment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets reckoning as provision: neither group is responsible for maintaining the other, since his reading of 78:36 describes a complete, sufficient gift.

MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the people who pray at dawn and evening as worshippers Bilal and Ibn Umm Ma'bad, who sat with the Prophet; Quraysh said they would join him if not for such low-status companions, so the Prophet was forbidden to expel them.

MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.claim: Abu Talib suggested Muhammad dismiss his poor followers so the nobles might follow him, but the verse forbade turning away those who pray for God.

MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.claim: The dawn and evening prayers were then two units each; the five daily prayers were prescribed later.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.claim: After commanding warning of the non-pious, God commands drawing the pious near and forbids their dismissal.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.claim: Calling on God morning and evening means continuous worship, or specifically dawn and afternoon prayers, or all five prayers; the Shami reading has the stated form of 'morning.'

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.claim: Seeking God's face means sincerity; 'face' can denote a thing's essence and reality.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.claim: Revelation followed the chiefs' demand to dismiss poor believers Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, and others; the Prophet refused, they requested alternate days and a written agreement, then the poor moved aside as Ali was called to write. The Prophet threw away the paper and embraced them.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.claim: The believers' account is theirs alone and cannot transfer to the Prophet; the source compares the statement with a verse about Noah's reckoning.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.claim: The consequence clause answers the negation, while the next clause answers the prohibition; alternatively, being unjust is caused by dismissing them.

ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.claim: Polytheists tried to make the Prophet dismiss poor followers so the elite would sit with him; they meant Suhayb, Khabbāb, ʿAmmār, Salmān, and Bilāl.

ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
